supersedes.reason: sensor.address has read 0x40 unchanged since v1, carried forward through v2/v3/v4 without ever being checked against the module actually on the bench. It is not the module's address: 2026-09-02 established via i2c.scan() that this unit's A0/A1 pins are strapped to answer at 0x44, not the 0x40 datasheet default (docs/INA226_SESSION_HANDOFF.md, 2026-09-02 entry). Separately, software/lib/ina226_capture.py's build_manifest() and validate_manifest() hardcode a sensor block ('ina226_logger v1', '0x40') that duplicates rather than reads the contract's own sensor block, and had silently drifted two versions behind it -- the real captures on disk were made with ina226_logger v2. Neither error is caught by any existing check: the frozen contract.sha256 in a manifest is compared only against the lib's own hardcoded CONTRACT_FORMAT/CONTRACT_PATH constants, never against a re-hash of the file those constants name, so a manifest can carry a hash of one contract version while its format/path fields claim another -- which is exactly the state build/ina226_capture/manifest.json was found in (sha256 of v4's bytes, format/path fields naming v3). This has to be corrected now: v3's own amendment reasoning applies verbatim -- a provenance field has no integrity if corrected after a session is sealed, and 0 sessions are sealed today.
supersedes.evidence: Found 2026-09-03 while re-reading the 2026-09-02 block-0 captures against the frozen validator: sha256(ina226_coarse_monitor_v4.json) == the sha256 already recorded in build/ina226_capture/manifest.json's contract block, while that same block's format/path fields read 'SPU_INA226_COARSE_MONITOR_V3' / the v3 path -- tools/ina226_capture_pipeline.py's DEFAULT_CONTRACT and software/tests/test_ina226_capture.py's CONTRACT constant were already pointed at v4 (an earlier, uncommitted step of the v3->v4 migration promised in v4's own 'EXECUTION NOTE' had gone further than its commit message says), but software/lib/ina226_capture.py's CONTRACT_FORMAT/CONTRACT_PATH constants, and its expected_sensor logger string, were never updated to match.
supersedes.scope: Corrective, not additive, and deliberately narrow: only sensor.address changes (0x40 -> 0x44). task, window, features, validation, safety, models, and gates are carried over from v4 unchanged -- same capture schema, same folds, same 3 classes, same 4 features, same normalization, same spu4_som_edge gate. sensor.logger was already correct in v4 (ina226_logger v2) and is unchanged here; only the code-side constants and hardcoded sensor copies that had drifted from it are being brought into line as part of the same fix, not the contract text.
supersedes.policy_note: address is provenance metadata only -- no code path compares a captured row against it, so this correction changes no computed value, gate, or prior result; it only makes the frozen record honest about which module produced the data. The corresponding code fix (software/lib/ina226_capture.py's CONTRACT_FORMAT/CONTRACT_PATH/expected_sensor, and tools/ina226_capture_pipeline.py's DEFAULT_CONTRACT) lands in the same commit as this file, and the real manifest is re-initialized against it before any further capture -- re-init is free today (0 sealed) and destroys all 30 hash slots if deferred past the first seal.

encoder.signal: raw rising-edge count per sample interval, not rpm
encoder.ppr_note: MUST be set to the measured value of the encoder actually used before any session is captured. A salvaged ball-mouse wheel and a bought encoder differ, and a raw count is meaningless without it. null here means undeclared, and a capture taken with it undeclared cannot be converted to rpm afterwards.
encoder.resolution_note: At 100 Hz a sample interval is 10 ms, so one edge is worth roughly 300 rpm on a 20-slot wheel -- per-row rotation is coarse by construction. Summed over the 32-sample window it is about 107 edges at 1000 rpm, roughly 1 percent. Aggregate before interpreting.

task.capture_order: block b uses class order rotated left by b modulo 3
task.session_vote: plurality over four windows; lowest class id breaks a tie

window.selection: first 128 rows; four contiguous non-overlapping windows

validation.bus_voltage_exemption: current_limited_stall is exempt because supply voltage collapse is the defining characteristic of that class, not a fault. Every other validation clause, including shunt scaling, shunt headroom, cadence, and row count, still applies to it in full.
validation.normalization: training-fold min/max affine map to 0..30000, round-half-even, held-out clamp with diagnostics
validation.session_leakage_policy: all four windows from one session remain in one fold
validation.pulses_note: pulses must be a non-negative integer on every accepted row. No class-conditional pulse gate is specified in v3, deliberately: it is not yet known whether a current-limited stall on this rig stops rotation completely or merely slows it, and inventing a threshold before measuring would encode a guess as a validation rule. The first capture block answers that empirically; a gate may be added in a later amendment IF sessions are still unsealed at that point.
validation.pulses_absent_is_not_encoder_absent: An all-zero pulse column is indistinguishable from a stalled motor, which is a real capture class. It does NOT prove the encoder was disconnected, and disconnection cannot be detected from the data. Confirm the encoder counts before capturing block 0.

safety.target: separate low-voltage actuator or fan; never an FPGA rail
safety.supply: current-limited bench supply with limit at or below the actuator continuous-current rating
safety.supply_limit_verification: The commanded limit must be verified against a measurement, not read from the front panel. A supply displaying 280 mA was measured regulating at 307.4 mA on 2026-08-06, above the actuator continuous rating it was set to protect.
abort_conditions: operator cannot confirm the actuator current rating

models.threshold: training-fitted scalar normal-versus-anomaly threshold with deterministic tie breaks
models.som: seven-node SPU_SOM_MAP_V1 with the published deterministic v1 schedule
models.ambiguity: the v1 hardware flag means exact zero winner/runner-up gap; report all gaps and exact ties
models.spu4_som_edge: four-node winner-take-all deterministic classifier (hardware/rtl/core/spu4/spu4_som_edge.v), no topology/neighbor diffusion unlike the seven-node SOM. Trained via tools/spu4_som_edge_trainer.py (exact-integer dyadic competitive learning), same frozen folds/session grouping/normalization as the seven-node path above. BMU selection uses software/lib/spu4_som_edge_oracle.py's find_bmu_edge, the same function the RTL is checked against bit-exactly.
models.spu4_som_edge_ambiguity_note: spu4_som_edge_wrapper.v's v1 ABI (best_node, best_quadrance) does not expose a runner-up node or gap, unlike the SOM1 evidence frame's confidence gap. No ambiguity gate is defined for spu4_som_edge; this is an honest hardware-ABI boundary, not an oversight.

gates.failure_policy: Record a negative result; do not tune the frozen capture, feature, fold, model, or gate contract against held-out scores. This applies independently to the seven-node SOM gates and the spu4_som_edge gates -- a negative on one is not grounds to relax the other's threshold.
